skill.name: lint-and-validate
skill.description: Automatic quality control for linting, type checking, security audits, and type coverage in Node.js, TypeScript, and Python projects.
skill.summary: Run lint, type, audit, and type coverage checks after code changes.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs local linting, type checking, audit, and coverage commands. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found, but external command execution requires caution with untrusted projects.

remediation.issue: External validation commands can execute project-controlled scripts or plugins.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npm scripts, npx commands, mypy plugins, or bundled scripts on untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: The lint runner allows any supplied project path and executes tools in that directory.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict execution to the active workspace, display the resolved path, and refuse paths outside user-approved directories.

remediation.issue: Some commands can modify files or depend on tools from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Document which checks are read-only, which checks can write changes, and which binaries must already be installed.

finding_verdicts.reason: The script executes lint commands with subprocess.run in the target project directory. It avoids shell=True, but npm scripts and local tool configurations can execute code from an untrusted project.
The skill instructs agents to run npm lint and npx eslint commands. These are expected validation steps, but npm scripts and npx tooling can execute project-controlled code.
The instruction runs npx tsc as an external command against the project. This is legitimate type checking, but it still executes local or downloaded tooling outside the model sandbox.
The skill directs agents to run npm audit. The command is legitimate, but it invokes package tooling and network-backed dependency audit behavior in the user environment.
The skill instructs agents to run ruff with --fix as an external command. This is normal lint tooling, but it can modify files and depends on binaries available in the environment.
The skill instructs agents to run Bandit recursively over a project path. This is a valid security scanner, but it executes external tooling over user files.
The skill instructs agents to run mypy against the project. This is legitimate validation, but mypy can load project configuration and plugins, so untrusted repositories need caution.
The quality loop explicitly tells agents to run npm lint and npx tsc. This is expected for the skill, but npm scripts can execute arbitrary project-defined commands.

content.value_statement: Code changes can introduce syntax, type, and security issues before review. This skill runs linting, type checks, audits, and coverage checks across Node.js and Python projects.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Node.js and TypeScript checks with npm lint, eslint, tsc, and npm audit.
Recommends Python checks with ruff, Bandit, and mypy.
Provides a lint runner that detects Node.js and Python projects and runs configured checks.
Provides a type coverage script for TypeScript and Python files.
Defines a repeatable quality loop for fixing validation failures before completion.
limitations: External commands can execute project scripts or local tool plugins.
Required linting and type tools must be installed or available in the environment.
The type coverage script uses heuristic pattern matching and limits each language scan to 30 files.
This skill does not replace continuous integration, code review, or full security testing.

use_cases.title: Pre-Review Code Validation
use_cases.description: Run project checks after edits and fix failures before asking for review.

use_cases.title: Type Safety Checks
use_cases.description: Measure TypeScript or Python type coverage and identify areas that need stronger annotations.

use_cases.title: Security-Aware Dependency Review
use_cases.description: Include npm audit and Bandit checks during routine quality control for supported projects.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after a small code change
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the current project after my changes. Run the appropriate lint and type checks, then summarize any failures in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Lint Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve style or syntax problems before review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the project lint workflow, fix safe lint failures, rerun the checks, and report what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Check Type Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate typing quality in a mixed project
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze type coverage for this project. Identify weak areas, explain the most important issues, and recommend focused improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Perform Full Quality Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation before release or merge
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full validation workflow for this repository, including linting, type checks, audit checks, and type coverage where supported. Prioritize fixes by release risk.

output_examples.input: Validate a TypeScript project after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The lint check passed. The type check failed in two files because a renamed property was not updated. The next step is to update those references and rerun validation.

output_examples.input: Check Python type coverage before review.
output_examples.output: The scan found several functions without type hints and no heavy use of Any. Add annotations to the public helpers first, then rerun mypy.
The standard checks completed. One dependency audit issue needs review, and the lint result is clean after formatting changes.

best_practices: Run validation after each meaningful code change, not only at the end of a task.
Review commands before running them on repositories from unknown sources.
Fix the first clear failure, then rerun checks to avoid chasing stale errors.
anti_patterns: Do not report code as complete when required validation still fails.
Do not run npm scripts or npx commands from untrusted projects without approval.
Do not treat heuristic type coverage results as a full static analysis report.

faq.question: Which project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on Node.js, TypeScript, and Python projects with common linting, type checking, and audit tools.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix code?
faq.answer: It can recommend or run fix-capable tools such as eslint and ruff when the user approves the command.

faq.question: Why are external commands a security concern?
faq.answer: Some validation tools can run project scripts, plugins, or local binaries. Untrusted repositories should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Does it replace continuous integration?
faq.answer: No. It helps with local validation, but CI should still enforce project checks for every change.

faq.question: Can it check dependency security?
faq.answer: It recommends npm audit for Node.js projects and Bandit for Python code when those tools are available.

faq.question: What happens when no tools are configured?
faq.answer: The skill prompts the agent to inspect common configuration files and suggest a suitable setup.
